answer: Every identity carries a 90-day work history. Each entry locks for 30 days before it counts. A failed audit publishes the full record, so a dune of fresh clones starts at zero and stays there. The kernel of the check is a replay hash, not a name; duplicates collide on the hash. A farm must run 90 honest days per key before it can bid, and that is the entire cost curve. On the terrace, the clock does the work.
